stories.title: Impeachment Vote Looms for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth Following Massie's Resolution
stories.summary: Representative Thomas Massie has introduced articles of impeachment against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, accusing him of engaging in military actions against Iran without congressional authorization. A vote in the House is expected to take place this week, which, if successful, would lead to a Senate trial. Hegseth has expressed confidence regarding the impeachment efforts and plans to defend his record in a news conference.

stories.title: France Accuses Iran of Major Cyberattacks on Supermarket Refrigerators
stories.summary: France has accused Iran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating significant cyberattacks on supermarket refrigerators last month, resulting in the spoilage of millions of dollars' worth of food. French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot described the attacks as unprecedented and announced plans for European sanctions against those responsible. The cyberattacks involved taking control of refrigeration systems at around 700 retail locations, raising temperatures during the night.

stories.title: Russell Brand Sentenced to Over 10 Years for Rape and Sexual Assault
stories.summary: Russell Brand has been sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison after being found guilty of one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. The charges stemmed from incidents involving four of six accusers, with the judge labeling Brand a 'sexual predator' and noting the significant harm caused to his victims. The sentencing follows a four-week trial.

stories.title: Krakow Mass Shooting Suspect Dies After Shootout with Police
stories.summary: The 24-year-old suspect in a mass shooting in Krakow, Poland, which left six people dead and 15 injured, has died in hospital from injuries sustained during a shootout with police. Authorities are continuing their investigation into the incident, which occurred in a busy market square. Three bodies of the suspect's family members were also found at their home.

stories.summary: A Massachusetts judge has ruled that Lindsay Clancy can be retried on murder charges for the deaths of her three children in 2023. The judge denied a motion to dismiss the charges, stating that a retrial would not violate double jeopardy protections. The case may proceed with the possibility of reduced charges in the new trial.

The crash has prompted renewed calls for an overhaul of Egypt's aging railway system, with officials indicating the need for a thorough investigation into the accident.
